title: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array
oneLinerQuestion: Find the starting and ending index of a given target value in a sorted array.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array problem requires locating the starting and ending index of a target value within a non-decreasing array in O(log N) time. A standard binary search terminates as soon as any occurrence of the target is encountered. Because duplicate target elements can span an arbitrary contiguous range, we instead execute two independent modified binary searches: one configured to continue searching left to pinpoint the first occurrence (lower bound), and another configured to continue searching right to pinpoint the last occurrence (upper bound).

- Step 1: Binary Search Boundary Helper — We design a helper function `findBound(isFirst)` that takes a boolean flag. We initialize search boundaries 'low = 0', 'high = nums.length - 1', and a tracker variable 'bound = -1'.

- Step 2: Finding the First Occurrence (Left Boundary) — When `isFirst` is true, we compute 'mid = Math.floor((low + high) / 2)'. If nums[mid] === target, we record 'bound = mid' as a valid candidate, but we do not stop; we deliberately eliminate the right side by setting 'high = mid - 1' to determine if an earlier matching instance exists to the left.

- Step 3: Finding the Last Occurrence (Right Boundary) — When `isFirst` is false, upon encountering nums[mid] === target, we record 'bound = mid' and greedily search the right half by setting 'low = mid + 1' to determine if a subsequent matching instance exists to the right.

- Step 4: Standard Range Discarding — For both search runs, standard monotonic rules apply: if nums[mid] < target, we search right via 'low = mid + 1'; if nums[mid] > target, we search left via 'high = mid - 1'.

- Step 5: Combining and Returning Bounds — We execute the search for the left index first: firstPos = findBound(true). If firstPos === -1 (indicating the target is entirely absent from the array), we can return [-1, -1] immediately without running the second search. Otherwise, we run lastPos = findBound(false) and return [firstPos, lastPos].

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(log N) because the algorithm runs at most two standard binary searches, each taking logarithmic time. Space Complexity: O(1) auxiliary space as only a few primitive pointer variables are used in memory.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION searchRange(nums, target):
    first = findBound(nums, target, True)
    IF first == -1 THEN RETURN [-1, -1]
    last = findBound(nums, target, False)
    RETURN [first, last]
END FUNCTION

FUNCTION findBound(nums, target, isFirst):
    low = 0, high = LENGTH(nums) - 1, idx = -1
    WHILE low <= high DO:
        mid = (low + high) / 2
        IF nums[mid] == target THEN:
            idx = mid
            IF isFirst THEN high = mid - 1 ELSE low = mid + 1
        ELSE IF nums[mid] < target THEN low = mid + 1
        ELSE high = mid - 1
    END WHILE
    RETURN idx
END FUNCTION
